claims.text: Depressive symptoms in adolescents increased yearly over a 4-year period.
Increased social media use is associated with higher depressive symptoms across individuals.
Increased computer use is associated with higher depressive symptoms across individuals.
Within-person annual increases in social media use are associated with concurrent increases in depressive symptoms.
Within-person annual increases in television viewing are associated with concurrent increases in depressive symptoms.
Associations between screen time, exercise, and self-esteem support the upward social comparison hypothesis over the displacement hypothesis.
Interaction between between-person and within-person associations concerning social media and self-esteem supports the reinforcing spirals hypothesis.

evidence.description: Depression symptoms increased from a year 1 mean of 4.29 points to a year 4 mean of 5.45 points.
For every increased hour spent using social media, adolescents showed a 0.64-unit increase in depressive symptoms (95% CI, 0.32-0.51).
Between-level associations for computer use showed a 0.69-unit increase in depressive symptoms per hour (95% CI, 0.47-0.91).
A further 1-hour increase in social media use in a given year was associated with a further 0.41-unit increase in depressive symptoms in that same year.
A within-person association was found for television viewing (0.18; 95% CI, 0.09-0.27).
Significant between-person and within-person associations between screen time and exercise and self-esteem supported upward social comparison and not displacement hypothesis.
A significant interaction between between-person and within-person associations concerning social media and self-esteem supported reinforcing spirals hypothesis.

methodologies.name: Multilevel modeling of longitudinal survey data
methodologies.description: Secondary analysis using multilevel models with random intercepts at school and individual levels to estimate between-person and within-person associations over 4 years.
datasets: Secondary analysis data from a trial assessing 4-year efficacy of a personality-targeted drug and alcohol prevention intervention
conditions: Sample of 3826 adolescents starting in 7th grade in 31 schools in Greater Montreal
Brief Symptoms Inventory for depression outcome

limitations.text: Longitudinal studies measuring the association between screen time and depression in adolescents are lacking.

future_work.text: Take both social media and television screen time modes into account when developing preventive measures and advising parents.
